newsitem.title: GUYANA: Flood of Guyanese mourners delay Jagan's cremation.
newsitem.headline: Flood of Guyanese mourners delay Jagan's cremation.

text.p: Family members of former Guyanese President Cheddi Jagan postponed his cremation on Tuesday as huge numbers of people arrived for a last look at his body.
Tens of thousands of mourners came from all over the country to the Albion Sports Ground, about 80 miles (130 km) east of Georgetown, where Jagan's body has been on display since late Monday.

Jagan, who died on Thursday of heart failure at the Walter Reed hospital in Washington, was due to be cremated on Tuesday afternoon at his birthplace Port Mourant, a few miles (kilometers) east of Albion. Jagan would have been 79 on March 22.
But the sheer weight of numbers wanting to see the country's most famous politician, obliged Jagan's family to delay the ceremony until Wednesday.

"We regret any inconvenience ... Pass the message on to family and friends planning to be at the cremation site that it has been postponed," Derek Jagan, brother of the former president and speaker of Parliament, said in a live address on national radio.
Jagan's death created the largest public outpouring of grief in the former British colony's history.
The tide of humanity at the Albion stadium was so great on Monday night that family members had to link arms around Jagan's casket to prevent the crowd from knocking it over.
"Be calm, be quiet, give President Jagan the respect and dignity he deserves," his widow Janet Jagan said on national radio.
Caribbean leaders attended a ceremony in the capital on Monday to pay their respects to a man who played a major role in Caribbean Cold War politics.
Cuba's President Fidel Castro sent a massage saying that Havana had lost a "great friend" and the Caribbean an "outstanding leader."
U.S. President Bill Clinton last week called Jagan "a champion of the poor."
A former Marxist and frequent visitor to Cuba, Jagan was Guyana's first prime minister when the Britain granted it self-government in 1961. He regained power with a surprise election victory in 1992.
Former prime minister and now interim president Samuel Hinds was sworn in immediately after Jagan's death and will lead the country until the next elections, probably in October.
